paragraphs: He is mentioned in Tanchuma, Chukat 22 (Buber edition), Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, fol. 38b (Buber edition), Pesikta Rabbati, section Parah, and Midrash Shmuel 13:8.
Hyman reports that Rabbi Yudan said [a teaching] in his name.

notes.text: The final letter in פ״יג-ת conflicts with the earlier OCR reading ח. The exact Midrash Shmuel locator and the Pesikta pagination remain to be checked.

The saved whole Krakow1893 Midrash Shmuel13 scalar at index7 (the eighth segment) juxtaposes full Rabbi Yudan and abbreviated R’ Mari bar Yaakov, without explicitly writing in his name. It supplies a corresponding13:8 passage alongside frozen פ״יג-ת, not proof that ת must be ח. Hyman owns the reporting formulation. Mari’s title remains R'; the named parallel supplies Yudan’s full title. Pesikta לח: and other uninspected references retain their prior limits.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 906) gives פ״יג־ח, where the supplied Hebrew has פ״יג־ת. Midrash Shmuel 13:8 puts Yudan and Mari bar Yaakov side by side. Buber’s Tanchuma, Chukat 22, and the Mandelbaum text of Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, section 4, explicitly say that Yudan reports in Mari bar Yaakov’s name. Buber’s Pesikta de-Rav Kahana, fol. 38b, has Yudan reporting in Rabbi Yaakov’s name, while note קנד records the fuller name from the Oxford manuscript and Yalkut Tehillim. In Pesikta Rabbati, section Parah (14), the consulted passage reads Mari Yaakov.
